stem: Why should an IPM record include the location and date of a finding rather than only the pest or symptom name?
choices: Spatial and temporal information helps reveal hotspots, spread, entry pathways, recurrence, and response to interventions
Dates are useful only for harvest planning
Locations are unnecessary if a pest has been seen once
Recording location prevents the need for future scouting
rationale: IPM decisions improve when findings can be analyzed across space and time. Location and date support trend analysis, hotspot mapping, and evaluation of interventions.
